checked_claims.note: Reconstructed and re-derived end to end. (i) M=ω^2⊗W_5^∨ has deg M = 2(2g-2) - (4g+12-4f)|_{g=6,f=5} = 20-16 = 4 and h^0(L)=1+h^0(M) by χ(L)=1 plus Serre duality; M is always special since h^1(M)=h^0(L)≥1. (ii) h^0(L)=4 gives h^0(M)=3 = deg M/2 + 1, i.e. Clifford equality with deg M ∉ {0,2g-2}, forcing C hyperelliptic and M≅(g^1_2)^{⊗2}. (iii) Castelnuovo–Severi: a degree-2 and a degree-4 map to P^1 not factoring through a common map give g ≤ (2-1)(4-1)=3 < 6; the common factor φ has deg φ | 2 and deg φ ≥ 2, so φ = h and γ = q∘h with deg q = 2. (iv) Splitting obstruction: h_*O_C = O⊕O(-7) (branch degree 2g+2=14); q_*O(-7) = O(-4)^2 is forced for EVERY degree-2 q, since deg = -8 by χ and h^0(q_*O(-7)⊗O(3)) = h^0(O(-1)) = 0 pushes the larger summand to ≤ -4; hence E = O(1)⊕O(4)^2, Sym^2E(-6) = O(-4)⊕O(-1)^2⊕O(2)^3 with h^0 = 9, and h^0(C,R⊗γ^*O(-6)) = 7 for R = O_{P(E^∨)}(2)|_C. Left-exactness gives h^0(F(-6)) ≥ 9-7 = 2, while balanced F = O(4)⊕O(5) gives F(-6) = O(-2)⊕O(-1) with h^0 = 0. The contradiction stands; every number was independently recomputed and agreed. The parenthetical 'does not require the weak relative-canonical normalization' is also true, but not for the reason written — see FC-0135-A.

Under the stated normalization M ≅ γ^*O(1) = O(D), so h^0(M) ≥ 2 (γ^* is injective on H^0(P^1,O(1))) and h^0(M) ≤ 3 by Clifford, i.e. h^0(L) ∈ {3,4}; CLM-0086-1 removes 4, leaving h^0(L)=3 on every geometric fibre — consistent with the internal cross-check that |L| is then a g^2_6 whose residual ω⊗L^{-1} is exactly the degree-4 pencil. The second half is correctly hypothesis-guarded: B reduced with h^0 constant = 3 are precisely Grauert's hypotheses, so p_*L is locally free of rank 3 with base change, and the Abel–Jacobi model Hilb^6 ×_{Pic^6} B ≅ P((p_*L)^∨) is Zariski-locally trivial because the projectivization of a locally free rank-3 sheaf is. The reducedness restriction honors the nonreduced-base obstruction, and the statement stays over schemes rather than silently widening to a stack base, so neither a constant-rank lifting argument nor a smooth-atlas descent line is owed. No coarse-versus-stack, integral-coefficient, cohomological-versus-BM-degree, Tate-twist, Gysin/Künneth, differential, invariants-versus-coinvariants, or semisimplification step occurs anywhere in this lemma; purity, Tate support, Tate assembly and RED-0001 are explicitly excluded and resolves_exact_target=false is recorded.

scope.generality: every smooth hyperelliptic genus-six curve and every degree-two q, over any characteristic-zero field

finding_candidates.statement: The exclusion of balanced CE relations on a genus-six hyperelliptic degree-four cover needs neither an explicit curve model nor the CE relative-canonical normalization. For γ = q∘h, E = O(1)⊕O(4)^2 is forced for EVERY degree-2 map q, because deg q_*O(-7) = -8 by Euler characteristic and h^0(q_*O(-7)⊗O(3)) = h^0(O(-1)) = 0 pushes the larger summand to degree ≤ -4. Given only that, h^0(Sym^2E(-6)) = 9, while h^0(C, O_{P(E^∨)}(2)|_C ⊗ γ^*O(-6)) = 7 follows from degree alone (deg = 36 - 24 = 12 > 2g-2 = 10, so h^1 = 0 and Riemann–Roch gives 7), with no identification of the line bundle and hence no use of O_{P(E^∨)}(1)|_C ≅ ω_{C/P^1}. Left-exactness then gives h^0(F(-6)) ≥ 2, excluding splitting types (4,5) and (3,6) among a+b=9.
finding_candidates.why_reusable: It upgrades a splitting-type fact whose recorded verification is a single explicit model (y^2 = f_14(x), z = x^2) to a model-free, normalization-free inequality, so downstream artifacts may invoke it on an arbitrary hyperelliptic fibre of an arbitrary family without re-choosing coordinates and without carrying the weak-normalization hypothesis into the exclusion step. It also shows the exclusion covers the adjacent (3,6) stratum, not only the balanced one.

finding_candidates.caveat: Not proved or asserted by the reviewed artifact; this is the reviewer's derivation from the confirmed h^0(L)=3 plus the packet's recorded base-point analysis and characteristic-zero Bertini. It says nothing about relative (as opposed to fibrewise) density over a general base, nothing about S_6 monodromy, and nothing about Tate type. Remains a candidate until independently corroborated.

scope.generality: geometric fibres of a balanced genus-six degree-four CE family satisfying the weak relative-canonical normalization

finding_candidates.statement: On a balanced fibre satisfying the weak CE normalization, h^0(L) = 3 (this lemma) combines with base-point-freeness of L on the balanced locus to make the general member of |L| ≅ P^2 consist of six DISTINCT points, hence the reduced-support open of the closed Abel–Jacobi incidence is nonempty and dense in every fibre of the P^2-bundle. Argument: if L had a base point p, then L(-p) would be a g^2_5 on a genus-six curve, forcing a smooth plane quintic, whose tetragonal pencil is projection from that point and is CE-unbalanced, hence excluded from the balanced locus; L base-point-free with h^0 = 3 gives a finite morphism φ_L : C → P^2 whose image spans, and in characteristic zero φ_L is separable onto its image, so a general line pulls back to a reduced divisor (Bertini), i.e. six distinct points.
finding_candidates.why_reusable: Fibrewise nonemptiness of the reduced-support open is a standing obstacle for the ordered Conf_6 model, and ATT-0086 explicitly disclaims it while in fact supplying the missing constancy input. If corroborated, the ordered/unordered S_6-torsor model acquires a nonempty base on every balanced normalized fibre with no further geometric input.

STRONGEST ATTACK — duality/sign flip in the CE quadratic-relation sequence. The whole contradiction is asymmetric in the convention: it requires the packet's F (the bundle whose balanced value is O(4)⊕O(5)) to be the KERNEL of Sym^2E → γ_*R, of degree +9. Much of the CE literature writes the degree-4 resolution with middle term π^*F^∨⊗O(-2), under which the pushed-forward relations bundle is the degree -9 dual. Had the packet meant that one, the hyperelliptic value would be O(-2)⊕O(-7), whose twist by -6 has h^0 = 0 exactly like the balanced O(-4)⊕O(-5): the contradiction would evaporate and the proof would be vacuous. This attack fails. Euler characteristics pin the orientation: χ(Sym^2E) = 4·deg E + 6 = 42 and χ(γ_*R) = χ(R) = 36 + 1 - 6 = 31, so the kernel has rank 2 and degree exactly +9 = deg(O(4)⊕O(5)), and the packet's own W-convention (deg W_f = 36 - 4f with f ∈ {4,5}, i.e. F^∨ = O(-4)⊕O(-5)) selects the same positive-degree bundle. Both splitting types under comparison, balanced (4,5) and hyperelliptic (2,7), have degree 9, so the comparison is internally consistent and the sign is right.

RUNNER-UP — a normalization leak inside the claim that no normalization is needed. CLM-0086-1 asserts the h^0=4 exclusion is independent of the weak relative-canonical normalization, yet the written derivation routes the target of the restriction map through H^0(C, A^6) with A = h^*O(1), an identification that uses ω_C = A^5 together with O_{P(E^∨)}(1)|_C ≅ ω_{C/P^1} — the very normalization being disclaimed. The claim nonetheless survives, for a reason the artifact does not state: deg(R⊗γ^*O(-6)) = 36 - 24 = 12 > 2g-2 = 10, so h^1 = 0 and h^0 = 12 - 6 + 1 = 7 by Riemann–Roch alone, whatever the line bundle is. Since the theorem_statement carries the normalization as a hypothesis anyway, this touches only an auxiliary parenthetical, not the theorem. Recorded as FC-0135-A.

(a) Castelnuovo–Severi yields only non-independence, not factorization through the hyperelliptic map; the missing line is that the common factor has degree dividing 2 and ≥ 2, hence equals h with residual map of degree 1 — correct, though compressed to one sentence. (d) Grauert was probed for the nonreduced-base failure mode; the theorem restricts to reduced B and does not widen to a stack base. (e) 'Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle' was probed for a hidden Brauer/twisted-form obstruction; there is none, since P of a locally free rank-3 sheaf trivializes wherever that sheaf does. (f) The lemma was probed for the standard campaign failure modes — stack versus coarse moduli, integral versus rational coefficients, cohomological versus Borel–Moore degree, Poincaré twists, Gysin and Künneth shifts, spectral-sequence differentials, Aut(Γ) invariants versus coinvariants, semisimplification versus honest Hodge isomorphism, predicted motives, pure-Tate-to-tautological upgrades, omitted stable pairs — and none arises, because the artifact makes no cohomological assertion at all. The correct residual reading is scope, not error: this lemma advances the geometry/computation node only, discharges no Tate obligation, and its novelty is modest, since FND-0104 and FND-0125 already compose to B_4 = ∅; what is new is the normalization-free route to hyperellipticity and the model-free splitting count.
theorem_statement: Let B be a reduced locally Noetherian scheme over a characteristic-zero field carrying a smooth genus-six degree-four Casnati–Ekedahl family whose relations bundle is fibrewise balanced, F_b ≅ O(4) ⊕ O(5), and which satisfies the weak CE relative-canonical normalization used in ATT-0066. For the canonical quotient W_5 put L=W_5⊗ω^{-1}. Then h^0(C_b,L_b)=3 for every geometric b in B; equivalently, the jump stratum B_4={b:h^0(L_b)=4} is empty. Consequently the closed degree-six Abel–Jacobi incidence Hilb^6(C/B)×_{Pic^6(C/B)}B is a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle over B. Thus a proposed balanced component decomposition containing a nonempty B_4/P^3 piece is false.
